prompt: Joyce has a box with light bulbs, some blue and some red. She counts the bulbs and finds that 10 of the 40 are blue. What percentage of the bulbs are blue?
If $2016\times x$ is a perfect square, what is the smallest positive integer value for $x$?

solutions.title: Prime factorisation
solutions.body:
$2016=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot7$. A perfect square needs every exponent even, so $x$ must contain one more $2$ and one $7$. The smallest is $x=2\cdot7=14$, giving $2016\cdot14=168^2$.

**Answer: 14**

prompt: For two positive real numbers $a$ and $b$, which may be equal, what is the smallest possible value of $\dfrac ab+\dfrac ba$?

solutions.title: Complete the square
solutions.body:
$\dfrac ab+\dfrac ba=\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{ab}=2+\dfrac{(a-b)^2}{ab}\ge2$, with equality when $a=b$.

**Answer: 2**

solutions.title: AM-GM
solutions.body:
For positive numbers, $\dfrac ab+\dfrac ba\ge2\sqrt{\dfrac ab\cdot\dfrac ba}=2$, with equality for $a=b$.

**Answer: 2**

prompt: In the four corners of the big square in the figure, squares with areas 9, 16, 25 and 49 are shaded. The two larger squares are touching. What is the area of the unshaded part of the big square?

solutions.title: Find the big square
solutions.body:
The shaded squares have sides $3,4,5,7$. The two larger squares (sides $7$ and $5$) are side by side along one side of the big square, so its side is $7+5=12$ and its area is $144$. The unshaded area is $144-(9+16+25+49)=144-99=45$.

**Answer: 45**

prompt: The lengths of all sides of a triangle are prime numbers. If two sides are 5 and 7 what is the longest possible length of the third side?

solutions.title: Triangle inequality
solutions.body:
The third side must be less than $5+7=12$. The largest prime below $12$ is $11$, and $5,7,11$ does form a triangle ($5+7>11$ and $11<5+7$, $7<5+11$).

**Answer: 11**

prompt: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius. On the SAMO scale, water freezes at 20 degrees and boils at 170 degrees. The two scales are linearly related. What is the temperature on the SAMO scale if it is 80 degrees on the Celsius scale?

solutions.title: Interpolate
solutions.body:
$80^\circ$C is $80\%$ of the way from freezing to boiling. On the SAMO scale the range is $170-20=150$, so the reading is $20+0.8\times150=140$.

**Answer: 140**

prompt: Each of the nine paths in a park is 100 m long. Ann wants to go from $X$ to $Y$ without going along any path more than once. What is the length, in metres, of the longest route she can choose?

solutions.title: Euler trail argument
solutions.body:
The network has $6$ junctions; every junction (corners and edge midpoints) is met by an even number of paths ($2$ or $4$). A walk from $X$ to $Y$ that uses a set of paths needs $X$ and $Y$ to meet an odd number of used paths and every other junction an even number. $X$ and $Y$ each meet only $2$ paths, so a walk from $X$ to $Y$ uses exactly one of them at each end; the unused paths therefore meet $X$ and $Y$ an odd number of times and every other junction an even number of times, which forces at least a connection from $X$ to $Y$: at least two unused paths (the two along the side $XY$ work). The remaining seven paths can be walked from $X$ to $Y$. The maximum is $7\times100=700$ m.

**Answer: 700**

prompt: How many two-digit positive integers $N$ have the property that the sum of $N$ and the number obtained by reversing the order of the digits of $N$, is a perfect square?

solutions.title: Sum is 11 times digit sum
solutions.body:
If $N=10x+y$ then $N+\text{reverse}=11(x+y)$. This is a perfect square only if $11\mid(x+y)$ with $11(x+y)$ square, i.e. $x+y=11$ (as $1\le x+y\le18$), giving $121$. The pairs are $(2,9),(3,8),(4,7),(5,6),(6,5),(7,4),(8,3),(9,2)$: $29,38,47,56,65,74,83,92$, so $8$ numbers.

**Answer: 8**

prompt: The faces of a cube are labelled with 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, so that the numbers on opposite faces add up to 9, as shown in Figure 1. When four such cubes are placed as shown in Figure 2 the numbers on each pair of touching faces add up to 10. Which number is represented by the $*$?

solutions.title: Follow the touching faces
solutions.body:
Opposite faces add to $9$ and touching faces add to $10$. The cube whose outer face shows $3$ has $6$ on its opposite (touching) face, so the face it touches is $4$, whose opposite face is $5$; that touches a $5$, and so on along the chain. The last touching pair is $7$ and $3$, so the face carrying $*$ is opposite a $3$ and $*=9-3=6$.

**Answer: 6**

reviewNote: Solution follows the official key; the arrangement of cubes in Figure 2 was not independently checked.

prompt: Let $P$ be the product of any three consecutive positive odd integers. What is the highest common factor (greatest common divisor) of all such numbers $P$?

solutions.title: Divisibility
solutions.body:
Among three consecutive odd integers exactly one is a multiple of $3$ (their differences are $2$ and $4$, so they cover all residues mod $3$), so $3\mid P$ always. Also $1\cdot3\cdot5=15$ and $7\cdot9\cdot11=693=3\cdot 231$ have $\gcd(15,693)=3$. So the highest common factor is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

prompt: If $AB$ is equal to the radius of the circle, what is the value of $\angle ACB$, in degrees?

solutions.title: Inscribed angle
solutions.body:
Let $O$ be the centre. Then $OA=OB=AB$, so $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral and $\angle AOB=60^\circ$. The inscribed angle on the same chord, $\angle ACB$, is half the central angle: $30^\circ$.

**Answer: 30**

prompt: If $f(x)=2^x$, what is the value of $\dfrac{f(x+1)+f(x)}{f(x)}$?

Simon and Harry spun a coin 30 times. Whenever the coin showed heads, Simon gave two sweets to Harry. When the coin showed tails, Harry gave three sweets to Simon. After 30 spins, both Simon and Harry had the same number of sweets as they started with. How many times did the coin show tails?

solutions.title: Balance the sweets
solutions.body:
Let tails appear $t$ times, so heads appear $30-t$ times. Simon receives $3t$ sweets and gives $2(30-t)$. These are equal: $3t=60-2t$, so $t=12$.

**Answer: 12**

prompt: What is the minimum number of integers which must be removed from the first 50 positive even integers so that the sum of the remaining integers is 2016?

solutions.title: Remove the largest numbers
solutions.body:
The first $50$ even integers sum to $2+4+\cdots+100=50\cdot51=2550$. We must remove numbers with sum $2550-2016=534$. The five largest, $100+98+96+94+92=480<534$, so five numbers are not enough, but six are: remove $100,98,96,94,92$ and $54$ (sum $534$). The minimum is $6$.

**Answer: 6**

prompt: Triangle $BCD$ lies in the plane, and $A$ is a point outside the plane. $AB$ is perpendicular to the plane and $BD$ is perpendicular to $CD$. What is $\angle ADC$ in degrees? (The lengths marked in the figure are $AB=\sqrt3$, $BD=1$, $CD=\sqrt3$.)

solutions.title: Pythagoras in 3D
solutions.body:
In the plane, $BC^2=BD^2+CD^2=1+3=4$. Since $AB$ is perpendicular to the plane, $AD^2=AB^2+BD^2=3+1=4$ and $AC^2=AB^2+BC^2=3+4=7$. Then $AD^2+DC^2=4+3=7=AC^2$, so by the converse of Pythagoras $\angle ADC=90^\circ$.

**Answer: 90**

prompt: $D$ is a point on side $AB$ of $\triangle ABC$, $E$ is a point on $CD$ and $F$ is a point on $CE$. The areas of triangles $AED$, $AEC$, $BFD$ and $BFC$ are 6, 10, 17 and 7, respectively. What is the area of $\triangle BEF$?

solutions.title: Ratios of areas on a line
solutions.body:
Triangles with the same apex and bases on line $DC$ have areas in the ratio of their bases. From apex $A$: $DE:EC=6:10$, so $DE=\frac{3}{8}DC$. From apex $B$: $DF:FC=17:7$, so $DF=\frac{17}{24}DC$. Then $EF=DF-DE=\frac{17-9}{24}DC=\frac13DC$. Triangle $BDC$ has area $17+7=24$, so $[BEF]=\frac13\cdot24=8$.

**Answer: 8**

prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ the sides $a$ and $b$ are not equal, and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. The numbers $x$ and $y$ are real, such that $\dfrac{x}{2a^2}+\dfrac{y}{c^2}=1$ and $\dfrac{x}{c^2}+\dfrac{y}{2b^2}=1$. What is the value of $x+y$ if $c=3$?

solutions.title: Subtract the equations
solutions.body:
Clearing fractions: $c^2x+2a^2y=2a^2c^2$ and $2b^2x+c^2y=2b^2c^2$. Subtract: $(c^2-2b^2)x+(2a^2-c^2)y=2c^2(a^2-b^2)$. By Pythagoras $c^2=a^2+b^2$, so $c^2-2b^2=2a^2-c^2=a^2-b^2\ne0$. Dividing by $a^2-b^2$: $x+y=2c^2=18$.

**Answer: 18**

prompt: What is the remainder when $2^{2016}$ is divided by 13?

solutions.title: Fermat
solutions.body:
By Fermat's little theorem $2^{12}\equiv1\pmod{13}$, and $12\mid2016$.

**Answer: 1**

prompt: The diagram shown is formed by extending the sides of a right triangle and constructing four circles that are each tangent to all three sides. The radii of the three smaller circles with centres at $D$, $E$ and $F$ are respectively equal to 3, 4 and 21. What is the length of the radius of the circle with centre $G$?

solutions.title: Incircle and excircles
solutions.body:
Let the triangle have right angle at $B$, legs $AB=p$, $BC=q$, hypotenuse $AC=h$ and semi-perimeter $s$. The circle $D$ is the incircle; $E$ and $F$ are the excircles opposite $A$ and $C$; $G$ is the excircle opposite $B$. Use the fact that the tangent length from a vertex to the excircle opposite that vertex is $s$.

- Excircle $G$: its centre is equidistant from the lines $BA$ and $BC$, which are perpendicular, so its radius equals the tangent length from $B$: $\rho_G=s$.
- Excircle opposite $A$: the radius equals the tangent length from $B$, and the tangent length from $A$ is $p+\rho$, which equals $s$. So $\rho=s-p$. Likewise the excircle opposite $C$ has radius $s-q$.
- Incircle: tangent lengths from $B$ are $r$, so $(p-r)+(q-r)=h$ and $r=s-h$.

Hence $r+\rho_A+\rho_C=(s-h)+(s-p)+(s-q)=3s-2s=s=\rho_G$. So $\rho_G=3+4+21=28$.

**Answer: 28**

solutions.title: Product relation
solutions.body:
For a right triangle, $r\cdot\rho_G=(s-h)s=\text{area}$ (since $rs=$ area) and $\rho_A\rho_C=(s-p)(s-q)=\frac{h^2-(p-q)^2}{4}=\frac{pq}{2}=$ area. So $r\rho_G=\rho_A\rho_C$, i.e. $3\rho_G=4\cdot21$ and $\rho_G=28$.

**Answer: 28**
